chapters.summary: This chapter contains 42 verses and records Moses being caught up to a high mountain, seeing God face to face, and being shown the earth and its inhabitants. God identifies Moses as his son, speaks of his endless works, and declares his purpose and creation through the Only Begotten. Satan tempts Moses to worship him; Moses resists by calling on God, and Satan departs. God commissions Moses to deliver Israel, discusses worlds without number, commands Moses to write, and foretells restoration of his words.

This chapter contains 31 verses and records the Lord revealing to Moses the creation of heaven and earth in six days: light and darkness; the firmament and divided waters; dry land, seas, and vegetation; sun, moon, and stars; sea life and birds with a command to multiply; land animals; and the creation of man and woman in God’s image with dominion and provisions of plants for food.

This chapter contains 25 verses and records God finishing creation, resting, blessing and sanctifying the seventh day, and stating that creations are made spiritually before naturally. God forms Adam, plants the Garden of Eden, places the tree of life and the tree of knowledge, and describes Eden’s river and its four branches. Adam is commanded not to eat the forbidden tree, names animals, and Eve is created from his rib; marriage is instituted.

This chapter contains 32 verses and records the Lord’s account to Moses of Satan’s rebellion and casting down, Satan’s use of the serpent to beguile Eve, and Adam and Eve eating the forbidden fruit. It covers their awareness of nakedness, hiding, and God’s questioning. It states curses on the serpent, sorrow in childbirth, and a cursed ground with toil and death. Adam names Eve; God makes skins; they are expelled from Eden and cherubim guard the tree of life.

This chapter contains 59 verses and records Adam and Eve laboring, multiplying, praying, and receiving commandments to worship and offer firstlings; an angel explains sacrifice, and the Holy Ghost bears record. Adam and Eve teach their children; some follow Satan. Cain and Abel are born; their offerings differ; Cain murders Abel and is cursed, marked, and sent to Nod. Cain’s lineage, a city, and Lamech’s descendants are listed; secret oaths, violence, curses, and early preaching of the gospel are described.

This chapter contains 68 verses and records Adam calling his sons to repent; Seth’s birth and worship; a book of remembrance and priesthood; genealogies from Adam to Enoch; increasing wickedness, wars, and secret works; Enoch’s prophetic call, visions, and preaching in the land of Cainan; and God’s instructions to Adam on repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ’s name, the Holy Ghost, and Adam’s baptism and spiritual rebirth.

This chapter contains 69 verses and records Enoch’s visions and prophecy from Mahujah and mount Simeon, including peoples of Shum and Canaan, lands shown, and the command to preach repentance and baptize. It describes Zion becoming one heart, the City of Holiness, and being taken into heaven. Enoch sees Satan’s power, God and Enoch weeping, the Flood with Noah, the Son of Man’s crucifixion and resurrection, last-days tribulations, the New Jerusalem, and a millennial rest.

This chapter contains 30 verses and records Enoch’s age, Methuselah’s lineage and prophecy concerning Noah, and a famine and curse on the earth. It gives lifespans of Methuselah and Lamech and names Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. It describes “sons of God” and “sons of men,” rising wickedness, giants seeking Noah’s life, and Noah’s ordination and preaching of repentance and baptism. God limits man’s days, warns of floods, declares earth corrupt and violent, and announces destruction of all flesh.

This chapter contains 31 verses and records Abraham in Chaldea seeking the blessings of the fathers and priesthood rights amid his fathers’ idolatry. Priests attempt to sacrifice him on an altar near Potiphar’s Hill, but Jehovah delivers him by an angel, calls him to leave his kindred, and destroys the altar and priest. It recounts Egyptian origins through Ham and Egyptus, Pharaoh’s lineage and priesthood restriction, a famine in Chaldea, and preservation of patriarchal records.

This chapter contains 25 verses and records a famine in Ur, Haran’s death, and Abraham’s marriage to Sarai. The Lord commands Abraham to leave his country; Abraham travels with Lot and Terah to Haran, where Terah returns to idolatry. The Lord appears, identifies himself as Jehovah, and promises Abraham land, seed, priesthood, and blessings. Abraham departs Haran at age 62, builds altars at Jershon, Sechem, and near Bethel, receives a promise of Canaan, and heads toward Egypt, instructing Sarai to say she is his sister.

This chapter contains 28 verses and records Abraham using the Urim and Thummim to learn of stars and governing planets, including Kolob near God’s throne and differing times of reckoning. The Lord shows Abraham the sun, moon, and stars, promises to multiply his seed, and says Abraham will declare these words before Egypt. God reveals premortal intelligences, noble ones, Abraham’s foreordination, the plan to make an earth and prove spirits, and a choosing of the first volunteer to be sent; the second rebels and many follow him.

This chapter contains 31 verses and records the Gods organizing the heavens and the earth through six times: creating light and dividing day from night; forming an expanse called Heaven; gathering waters and bringing forth dry land; producing plants and fruit trees; setting sun, moon, and stars for signs, seasons, days, and years; creating sea life and birds and blessing them to multiply; creating land animals; and forming man and woman in their image, granting dominion and assigning plants for food.

This chapter contains 21 verses and records the Gods finishing creation, resting and sanctifying the seventh time, and forming the generations of heaven and earth. It describes mist watering the ground, the creation of man from dust with his spirit, and the planting of Eden with the tree of life and the tree of knowledge. It includes the command not to eat the forbidden tree, the creation of woman from Adam’s rib, marriage, nakedness without shame, and Adam naming animals.

This chapter contains 55 verses and records Jesus leaving the temple, foretelling its destruction, and teaching on the Mount of Olives about signs of his coming and the end: deception by false Christs and prophets, persecution, betrayal, wars, famines, pestilences, earthquakes, and worldwide preaching of the gospel. It covers the abomination of desolation and flight from Judea, great tribulation, cosmic signs, angels gathering the elect, parables of the fig tree and Noah, exhortations to watch, and the faithful and evil servant.

This chapter contains 75 verses and records Joseph Smith’s purpose for writing (1838), his birth and family moves to Palmyra and Manchester, and local religious revivals. It recounts his 1820 prayer and vision of two Personages, instruction to join no sect, and ensuing persecution. It covers Moroni’s 1823 visits about gold plates, Urim and Thummim, annual meetings, and warnings. It records obtaining and safeguarding the plates (1827), moving to Pennsylvania, early translation, Martin Harris’s Anthon visit, Oliver Cowdery as scribe, and John the Baptist conferring Aaronic Priesthood and commanding baptism (May 1829).

This chapter contains 13 verses and records thirteen Articles of Faith: belief in the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost; accountability for personal sin; salvation through Christ’s Atonement by gospel obedience; faith, repentance, baptism, and laying on of hands; divine calling and authority; church offices; spiritual gifts; scripture (Bible and Book of Mormon); continuing revelation; gathering of Israel, Zion, and Christ’s reign; religious freedom; civic obedience; and moral virtues and doing good.
